units.source_text: 源氏大将心甚恋慕藤壶皇后。

en.t: General Genji deeply yearned for Empress Fujitsubo.

units.source_text: 此时为欲惩诫她的冷酷，故意不理睬她，闭门隐忍度日。

en.t: At this time, wanting to punish her coldness, he deliberately ignored her and spent his days shut away in silent endurance.

units.source_text: 然而深恐外人看了不成样子，自己也寂寞无聊，因此发心赴云林院佛寺游览，乘便观赏秋野的景色。

en.t: Yet he feared that outsiders would think his conduct unseemly, and he himself was lonely and bored, so he resolved to visit the Buddhist temple at Unrin-in and take the chance to admire the autumn fields.

units.source_text: 亡母桐壶更衣的哥哥是个律师，就在这寺里修行。

en.t: The elder brother of his late mother, the Kiritsubo Intimate, was a risshi priest and was practicing at this temple.

units.source_text: 大将在这里诵经礼佛，滞留两三天，倒也很有趣味。

en.t: The general chanted sutras and worshiped the Buddha there, staying for two or three days, and found it unexpectedly pleasant.

units.source_text: 木叶渐次变红，秋野景色清丽，令人看了浑忘家乡。

en.t: The leaves were gradually turning red, and the clear beauty of the autumn fields made one forget home entirely.

units.source_text: 源氏大将召集一切有学问的法师，请他们说教，向他们问道。

en.t: General Genji gathered all the learned monks, asked them to preach, and questioned them about the Way.

units.source_text: 由于地点所使然，令人彻夜痛感人生之无常，直到天明。

en.t: Because of the place itself, everyone keenly felt the impermanence of human life through the night until dawn.

units.source_text: 然而正如古歌所云：“破晓望残月，恋慕负心人。”不免使他想起那意中人来。

en.t: Yet, just as the old poem says, "At daybreak, seeing the lingering moon, one longs for the heartless beloved," it inevitably made him think of the one he loved.

units.source_text: 将近天明，法师等在月光之下插花供水，发出杯盘叮当之声。

en.t: Near dawn, the monks arranged flowers and offered water beneath the moonlight, making the cups and trays ring softly.

units.source_text: 菊花和浓淡不同的各种红叶，散置各处。

en.t: Chrysanthemums and many kinds of red leaves in varying shades were scattered here and there.

units.source_text: 这景象也颇有趣致。

en.t: This scene too had considerable charm.

units.source_text: 源氏大将念念不忘地想：“如此修行，可使现世不致寂寞，

en.t: General Genji kept thinking, "If one practices in this way, this present life need not be lonely,

units.source_text: 又可使后世获得善报，这虚幻无常的一身还有什么烦恼呢？”

en.t: and in the life to come one may gain good recompense; what troubles can there be for this fleeting, impermanent body?"

units.source_text: 律师以尊严之声朗诵“念佛众生摄取不舍”。

en.t: The risshi priest recited in a solemn voice, "Those beings who recite the Buddha's name are embraced and never abandoned."

units.source_text: 源氏公子听了觉得深可羡慕，想道：“我自己何不决心出家呢？”

en.t: Prince Genji heard this and found it deeply enviable, thinking, "Why do I myself not resolve to leave the world?"

units.source_text: 此念一动，便首先挂念紫姬，真是道心不坚！

en.t: As soon as that thought arose, he first worried about Lady Murasaki; truly, his religious resolve was not firm.

units.source_text: 他觉得从来不曾如此长久离开紫姬，便频频写信去慰问她。

en.t: He felt that he had never before been away from Lady Murasaki for so long, and he repeatedly wrote letters to comfort her.

units.source_text: 有一封信中说：“我想尝试一下：脱离尘世是否可能？

en.t: In one letter he wrote, "I wished to try whether it might be possible to leave the world behind.

units.source_text: 然而无以慰我寂寥，反而更觉乏味。

en.t: Yet there is nothing to soothe my loneliness, and instead I feel all the more weary of it.

units.source_text: 但目下尚有听讲之事未了，一时不能返家。

en.t: But for the moment there are still lectures I must hear, so I cannot return home just yet.

units.source_text: 你处近况如何？念念。”

en.t: How are things with you now? I think of you constantly."

units.source_text: 随意不拘地写在一张陆奥纸上，非常美观。

en.t: It was written freely and without formality on a sheet of Michinoku paper, and it looked very beautiful.

units.source_text: 又附诗道：

en.t: He also added a poem, saying:
